title: Review a week of learning
description: Compare planned practice with actual work.
accomplishes: Compare planned practice with actual work. Identify one demonstrated gain, recurring confusion and a manageable next experiment. Separate effort from competence and avoid turning reflection into a punitive score or unsupported claim of progress.
prompt:
Act as a learning coach.

Task: Review a week of learning.

Input context:
- GOAL: [GOAL]
- PRACTICE LOG: [PRACTICE LOG]
- DIFFICULTIES: [DIFFICULTIES]
- EVIDENCE: [EVIDENCE]

Compare planned practice with actual work. Identify one demonstrated gain, recurring confusion and a manageable next experiment. Separate effort from competence and avoid turning reflection into a punitive score or unsupported claim of progress.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Weekly reflection example
The learner attempted three query exercises but still confuses filtering and grouping. Keep one corrected example, explain the distinction in their own words and plan a short follow-up task. Do not call the week a failure because the schedule changed. Progress must be supported by actual work, not assumed from time spent.
